reference: System Bash type/help builtins for metadata contracts; an independent Bash glob matcher for the simple shell patterns in a private modules.alias fixture; an independent Bash DFS over the documented modules.dep format; and GNU find/sort/mkdir/ln to encode the documented weak-updates symlink behavior. Synthetic info expectations follow the documented sysfs field/parameter contract. No reference expectation is copied from bashkmod output. The depmod output_deps implementation serializes all sorted transitive dependencies: https://github.com/kmod-project/kmod/blob/master/tools/depmod.c . Relative weak-updates links are independently constructed with GNU ln -sr and checked by dereferencing their fixture contents.
coverage: Bash builtin availability and public help metadata without invoking a module operation.
Fixture-only aliases wildcard matching and file-order output.
Fixture-only modules.dep dependency order, including compressed suffixes and nested dependencies, checked with an independent Bash DFS encoder.
weak-modules materialization of relative symlinks inside the private fixture tree.
info and --params against a synthetic BASHKMOD_SYS_MODULE_DIR tree.
Usable relative weak-updates targets with spaces, nested directories, dry-run preservation and repeated matching links.
exclusions: No real finit_module or delete_module calls, and no non-dry-run modprobe.
No live /proc/modules or /sys/module state; list and live info need a controlled disposable kernel.
No modprobe install/remove policy command execution.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must classify the statically registered bashkmod as a builtin; this checks metadata only.
Bash help must expose the documented bashkmod verbs and usage forms without invoking them.
cases.script:
doc=$(help bashkmod)
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod load PATH [PARAMS]"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod modprobe"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod resolve NAME"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod unload NAME"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod list"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod info"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod deps NAME"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod aliases MODALIAS"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod policy NAME"* ]]
[[ $doc == *"bashkmod weak-modules"* ]]
printf '%s\n' 'help contains all documented verbs'

cases.purpose: Match multiple fixture aliases using shell-style * patterns and preserve modules.alias file order; reference branch independently applies Bash glob matching.
cases.script:
modalias='pci:v00008086d00001234sv00000001sd00000002bc01sc02i03'
printf '%s\n' \
  '# private aliases fixture' \
  'alias pci:v00008086d00001234sv00000001* first_mod' \
  'alias pci:v00008086d00001234sv00000001sd00000002* second_mod' \
  'alias pci:v00008086d00001234sv00000001sd00000002bc* third_mod' \
  'options ignored-module debug=1' > modules.alias
if [[ $(type -t bashkmod) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHKMOD_MODULES_DIR=. bashkmod aliases "$modalias"
else
  while IFS=$' \t' read -r directive pattern module remainder; do
    if [[ $directive != alias || -z $pattern || -z $module ]]; then
      continue
    fi
    if [[ $modalias == $pattern ]]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$module"
    fi
  done < modules.alias
fi

cases.purpose: Resolve a one-level dependency using the documented modules.dep format and strip .ko.xz; the reference is an independent awk graph traversal.
cases.script:
printf '%s\n' \
  'kernel/driver/root.ko: kernel/driver/dep.ko.xz' \
  'kernel/driver/dep.ko.xz:' > modules.dep
target=root
if [[ $(type -t bashkmod) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHKMOD_MODULES_DIR=. bashkmod deps "$target"
else
  declare -A deps seen
  module_name() {
    local path=${1##*/}
    case "$path" in
      *.ko.zst) path=${path%.ko.zst} ;;
      *.ko.xz) path=${path%.ko.xz} ;;
      *.ko.gz) path=${path%.ko.gz} ;;
      *.ko) path=${path%.ko} ;;
    esac
    printf '%s\n' "$path"
  }
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    if [[ $line != *:* ]]; then continue; fi
    lhs=${line%%:*}
    rhs=${line#*:}
    owner=$(module_name "$lhs")
    deps[$owner]=$rhs
  done < modules.dep
  visit() {
    local name=$1 path dep
    if [[ ${seen[$name]+x} ]]; then return 0; fi
    seen[$name]=1
    for path in ${deps[$name]-}; do
      dep=$(module_name "$path")
      visit "$dep"
    done
    printf '%s\n' "$name"
  }
  visit "$target"
fi

cases.purpose: Materialize weak-updates links from a relative private module root. GNU find/sort/mkdir and ln -sr independently build usable links into the source tree; compare target strings as well as contents and modes.
cases.script:
root=fixture/modules
mkdir -p "$root/src/nested"
printf '%s\n' 'one' > "$root/src/z.ko"
printf '%s\n' 'two' > "$root/src/nested/a.ko.xz"
printf '%s\n' 'skip' > "$root/src/readme.txt"
if [[ $(type -t bashkmod) == builtin ]]; then
  BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT="$root" bashkmod weak-modules src dst
else
  srcdir="$root/src"
  dstdir="$root/dst/weak-updates"
  mkdir -p "$dstdir"
  while IFS= read -r srcpath; do
    rel=${srcpath#"$srcdir"/}
    dest="$dstdir/$rel"
    mkdir -p "${dest%/*}"
    printf 'ln -s %s %s\n' "$srcpath" "$dest"
    ln -sr "$srcpath" "$dest"
  done < <(find "$srcdir" -type f \( -name '*.ko' -o -name '*.ko.xz' -o -name '*.ko.gz' -o -name '*.ko.zst' \) -print | sort)
fi

cases.purpose: Read documented fields and alphabetically ordered parameters from a private synthetic sysfs-shaped tree; no live /sys or kernel module is used.
cases.script:
sysroot=fixture/sys-module
mkdir -p "$sysroot/demo/parameters"
printf '%s\n' 4096 > "$sysroot/demo/coresize"
printf '%s\n' live > "$sysroot/demo/initstate"
printf '%s\n' 0 > "$sysroot/demo/refcnt"
printf '%s\n' fixture-1 > "$sysroot/demo/version"
printf '%s\n' last > "$sysroot/demo/parameters/zeta"
printf '%s\n' first > "$sysroot/demo/parameters/alpha"
: > "$sysroot/demo/parameters/empty"
BASHKMOD_SYS_MODULE_DIR="$sysroot" bashkmod info demo
cases.stdout:
coresize=4096
initstate=live
refcnt=0
version=fixture-1
param.alpha=first
param.empty=
param.zeta=last

cases.purpose: Check the documented --params mode against the same synthetic sysfs contract, including sorting and empty parameter values.
cases.script:
sysroot=fixture/sys-module
mkdir -p "$sysroot/demo/parameters"
printf '%s\n' last > "$sysroot/demo/parameters/zeta"
printf '%s\n' first > "$sysroot/demo/parameters/alpha"

cases.purpose: Load/unload and non-dry-run modprobe mutate kernel module state.
cases.reason: Run only in a future disposable VM booted with a purpose-built test kernel and disposable modules, with CAP_SYS_MODULE and a snapshot/revert boundary. Compare load/unload state transitions with kmod insmod/rmmod/modprobe or a reviewed syscall mock that records finit_module and delete_module. The current fixture runner denies these syscalls, and host/kernel module changes are explicitly out of scope.

cases.purpose: bashkmod list reads the live /proc/modules file; live info reads kernel-owned sysfs state.
cases.reason: A future disposable VM or reviewed procfs/sysfs mock must provide a deterministic set of loaded test modules. Compare list output with lsmod and info fields with the corresponding synthetic/live sysfs values. The current list command has no path override for /proc/modules, and changing kernel module state to seed it is prohibited here.

cases.purpose: modprobe policy can select soft dependencies and may execute configured install/remove argv while applying module actions.
cases.reason: Use a future isolated modules tree plus a reviewed execve and module-syscall mock that records helper argv, dependency order, blacklist decisions, and load/unload requests. Compare planning with kmod modprobe --dry-run/--show-depends. Do not run against host modprobe.d files or a live kernel.

cases.purpose: Weak-updates links created from a relative private module root must resolve to the original file bytes. GNU ln -sr independently builds usable relative links; compare raw action rows, link targets and dereferenced bytes.
cases.script:
mkdir -p modules/src
printf 'module fixture bytes\n' > modules/src/a.ko
if [[ $(type -t bashkmod) == builtin ]]; then
 BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT=modules bashkmod weak-modules src dst
else
 mkdir -p modules/dst/weak-updates
 printf 'ln -s %s %s\n' modules/src/a.ko modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko
 ln -sr modules/src/a.ko modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko
fi
cat modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko

cases.purpose: Relative module roots containing spaces and a dot component still produce usable nested links with the same target bytes as independent GNU ln -sr. Only synthetic ordinary dummy module files are used.
cases.script:
root='module root/./parts'
mkdir -p "$root/src/nested"
printf 'dummy nested bytes\n' > "$root/src/nested/a.ko"
if [[ $(type -t bashkmod) == builtin ]]; then
 BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT="$root" bashkmod weak-modules src dst
else
 mkdir -p "$root/dst/weak-updates/nested"
 printf 'ln -s %s %s\n' "$root/src/nested/a.ko" "$root/dst/weak-updates/nested/a.ko"
 ln -sr "$root/src/nested/a.ko" "$root/dst/weak-updates/nested/a.ko"
fi
cat "$root/dst/weak-updates/nested/a.ko"

cases.purpose: The authorized branch dry run prints an action without creating destination paths; normal runs produce a usable relative link and accept that same matching link on a repeated call.
cases.script:
mkdir -p modules/src
printf 'dummy bytes\n' > modules/src/a.ko
actions=$(BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT=modules bashkmod weak-modules -n src dst)
[[ $actions == 'ln -s modules/src/a.ko modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko' && ! -e modules/dst ]]
BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT=modules bashkmod weak-modules src dst > first-actions
BASHKMOD_MODULES_ROOT=modules bashkmod weak-modules src dst > second-actions
[[ -L modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko ]]
IFS= read -r payload < modules/dst/weak-updates/a.ko
[[ $payload == 'dummy bytes' ]]
printf 'dry run and repeated relative link matched\n'
cases.stdout: dry run and repeated relative link matched
